objective: Make the archived quantum-code research instrument operational for valid general one-qubit-correcting codes with complex amplitudes, including nonorthogonal error sectors and genuine degeneracy, while preserving trace and explicitly reporting erasure outside the correctable subspace.
beneficiary: MONTREAL.AI internal computational quantum-code research; no physical device, quantum advantage, sale, or globally novel recovery algorithm is claimed.
deliverable: A self-contained Python module recovery.py exporting class Recovery; standard library, NumPy and SciPy only. No network, installed-code mutation, paid services, or additional packages.

inputs.codewords: Ordered orthonormal logical basis; dictionary integer keys 0..2**n-1 and finite complex amplitudes. Arbitrary complex sparse amplitudes, not restricted to nonnegative square roots. Qubit 0 is the most-significant bit.
inputs.qualified_domain: n <= 20, K in {2,4}, <=4096 initial nonzero code amplitudes; mathematically valid codes correcting arbitrary errors on any one physical qubit. The finite tested cohort is well conditioned at double precision. No claim of universal floating-point decisions at a singular threshold.
inputs.invalid_codes: Reject nonorthonormal codes or codes that fail single-qubit Knill-Laflamme conditions by a clearly resolvable amount, rather than silently normalize or report successful correction.

interface.encode: encode(logical) -> dict[int,complex]. Accept any finite K-component vector, preserve its norm, and return the ordered linear combination of supplied codewords. Do not normalize.
interface.recover: recover(branches: list[dict[int,complex]]) -> dict with logical_density (complex KxK array-like), input_probability (float), correctable_probability (float), erasure_probability (float). Each branch is an unnormalized pure-state Kraus component. Sum density contributions, never coherently add distinct branches. Zero and subnormalized inputs are valid; no hidden renormalization.
interface.kraus: kraus() -> list of recovery operators; each operator is a list of K sparse rows (dict[int,complex]). Row coefficients act as sum(row[word]*state[word]); coefficients are not implicitly conjugated. This exports a finite inspectable certificate of the logical recovery channel, without specifying how to construct it.

acceptance.scientific: For every tested logical state and any tested one-qubit CPTP channel, recover returns the original logical density and zero erasure within tolerance. This includes coherent rotations, genuinely complex Kraus operators, nonorthogonal full-rank error sectors and rank-deficient error sectors.
acceptance.complete_channel: Let S be the span of applying I and every single-qubit X,Y,Z to every codeword. The exported logical Kraus operators satisfy sum R_j^dagger R_j = projector onto S. The logical output is sum_j,b R_j|branch_b><branch_b|R_j^dagger. The orthogonal complement is mapped to one classical erasure flag, so output is blockdiag(logical_density, erasure_probability). This is a trace-preserving completely positive channel including erasure; no postselection or normalization.
acceptance.mass: input_probability=sum of raw branch squared norms; correctable_probability=real trace(logical_density); erasure_probability=input_probability-correctable_probability. Nonnegative up to tolerance and input/output mass conserved.
acceptance.certificate: Independent verification checks the exported operators, correctability, completeness on S, contraction on the full physical space and agreement with recover on fresh inputs. A successful visible example alone is insufficient.
acceptance.tolerance: Absolute error <=2e-8 * max(1,input_probability); independent certificate checks use the corresponding scale-aware spectral or entrywise tolerance.
acceptance.resources: CPU only; a candidate process may use up to 10 GiB RAM. Use sparse/active-coordinate representations: dense 2**n by 2**n physical operators are not an acceptable route. Run in an ordinary isolated scientific-Python subprocess, explicitly not the existing Forge stdlib/seccomp sandbox.

cases.purpose: Published nontrivial seven-qubit permutation-invariant code with nonzero common KL cross terms, full-rank error Gram matrix; it is nonorthogonal but not degenerate.
Nine-qubit Shor code with genuinely degenerate single-qubit error spaces.
The actual archived 15-qubit, four-dimensional controlled-S code; its existing zero-moment recovery domain must keep working.

development.example: public_fixtures.development_example(Recovery) supplies a small visible correction check.

procedure.construction: One initial construction and at most two development repairs, retaining every submitted source and visible result. Freeze final source before private qualification; private results may not drive repairs within this registered experiment.
procedure.withheld: Fresh valid variants, logical states, coherent and incoherent channels, erasure inputs, scale/branch invariances and invalid witnesses remain separate from builder context. Independent verifier will freeze all hidden material before first submission and will not inspect candidate implementation.
procedure.baselines: Compare the existing archived instrument on its proper domain and an independently implemented competent sparse canonical recovery route. Established mathematics and ordinary scientific libraries are allowed for all routes.
procedure.accounting: Record actual elapsed time, execution CPU/RSS where available, file hashes, failed attempts, integration and verification. Included-platform model usage and monetary costs are unknown unless exposed. Do not invent human labor or a price.
procedure.claims: Passing establishes useful installed computational recovery functionality. A distinct successor construction comparison and full accounting are still required for transfer or compounding claims.
